title: Desktop Outpost
tagline: Side quest: what to do when the thing you must test is not a web page.
teaches: pywinauto, the Windows accessibility tree, and how the same layering applies outside the browser
objectives: Say why Playwright cannot drive a native window, and what pywinauto does instead
Find a control by its accessibility name, the desktop cousin of get_by_role()
Apply the same layering off the web: tests assert, page objects own every control
Name what you give up outside the browser - no auto-waiting, no headless, no CI on a locked desktop
Decide when a desktop test is worth its cost, and when a unit test would do the job better
plannedChallenges: Why Playwright stops at the window frame
The accessibility tree, and how to look at it
Auto-waiting is gone: what replaces it
The same layering, a different driver
Quiz: when is a desktop test the right tool?
